content.value_statement: Organizations often lack a defensible path for recognizing data resources in financial statements. This skill structures the assessment, accounting treatment, disclosures, and audit evidence.
actual_capabilities: Screens data resources through compliance, quality, and value criteria.
Classifies qualifying resources as intangible assets, inventory, development expenditure, or current expenses.
Structures cost allocation, capitalization timing, amortization, and impairment approaches.
Drafts accounting treatment plans and financial statement disclosure text.
Creates evidence checklists and responses for common auditor questions.
Organizes a staged workflow from feasibility review through final delivery.
limitations: It does not replace licensed legal, valuation, accounting, or audit opinions.
Its conclusions depend on complete source, ownership, cost, quality, and usage evidence.
The knowledge base reflects rules and guidance identified through September 22, 2026.
It cannot verify documents, system records, signatures, or regulatory acceptance independently.

use_cases.title: Screen a Data Portfolio
use_cases.description: Identify which data resources are viable, need remediation, or should remain outside the balance sheet.

use_cases.title: Prepare Accounting Treatment
use_cases.description: Define account classification, capitalization boundaries, cost allocation, amortization, impairment, and disclosure requirements.

use_cases.title: Build an Audit Evidence Package
use_cases.description: Map assertions to source records, ownership evidence, approvals, calculations, and anticipated auditor questions.

prompt_templates.title: Initial Readiness Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether our data resource may qualify for capitalization. Ask for the essential facts, then classify it as viable, remediable, or unsuitable.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner screening before a formal project

prompt_templates.title: Account Classification Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare intangible asset, inventory, development expenditure, and expense treatment for this resource. Explain each criterion and list missing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Capitalization and Disclosure Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a treatment plan covering capitalization timing, eligible costs, allocation rules, amortization, impairment, journal-entry logic, and financial statement disclosures.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Challenge Simulation
prompt_templates.prompt: Challenge our proposed treatment as an external auditor. Identify weak assertions, request supporting evidence, propose adjustments, and draft defensible management responses.

output_examples.input: We developed an internal customer analytics dataset after January 2024. Can it be capitalized?
output_examples.output: Preliminary status: remediation required. Confirm lawful personal-information processing, control, technical feasibility, future benefits, development-stage timing, and directly attributable costs before recognition.

output_examples.input: Should a data product developed for routine sale be an intangible asset or inventory?
output_examples.output: Likely classification: inventory, when held for sale in ordinary operations. Document the sales model, control, cost records, expected benefits, and impairment policy.

output_examples.input: What should our audit package contain?
output: A resource inventory with source, ownership, classification, and responsible owner.
Evidence separating research costs from development costs and establishing the capitalization date.
Cost records, allocation rules, approvals, useful-life support, impairment analysis, and draft disclosures.

best_practices: Resolve source legality, personal-information compliance, and ownership before valuation or accounting design.
Link every conclusion and amount to dated evidence, responsible owners, and reproducible calculations.
Review current regulations and obtain licensed opinions before posting entries or issuing financial statements.
anti_patterns: Do not capitalize data collection costs without separating research and qualifying development activities.
Do not select useful lives, allocation methods, or values without documented support.
Do not present preliminary guidance as regulatory approval, audit acceptance, or a guaranteed financing outcome.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee that a data resource can be capitalized?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured assessment, while management, licensed advisers, auditors, and regulators retain decision authority.

faq.question: Which accounting categories does it evaluate?
faq.answer: It evaluates intangible assets, inventory, development expenditure, and current-period expense treatment.

faq.question: Can it determine the capitalization amount?
faq.answer: It can structure eligible costs and allocation methods, but the amount requires verified records and professional review.

faq.question: Does capitalization create profit?
faq.answer: No. Capitalization changes expense timing and creates future amortization or impairment exposure.

faq.question: Can it handle data containing personal information?
faq.answer: It can identify compliance questions, but qualified privacy and legal specialists must confirm lawful processing and ownership.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the resource inventory, sources, rights, intended use, development timeline, cost records, quality evidence, and expected economic benefits.
